what: The conclusions this tool published, or nearly published, and which were wrong.
why: Every measurement page shows what the measured system gets wrong. Almost none shows what the measurement itself got wrong. Yet that is the only evidence a figure was ever put to the test, and the only history a model validator can audit.
caughtBeforeAnyoneSawIt_definition: True when the claim was withdrawn BEFORE reaching anyone outside the people who wrote it: before publication, before being said to someone, before going online. False as soon as it was published, spoken or read by a third party — however briefly, and however few the readers. An internal page two people read counts as seen. Where the reach is uncertain, mark false: the error then goes toward shrinking the flattering count, never toward inflating it.

entries.headline: The hand-written rules seemed perfect on all five fields; they had been graded against the very templates used to write them.
entries.claimed: The hand-written rules score 100 % on all five fields.
entries.actually: They score 0 % on two of them. The regexes had been written against the very templates used to grade them.
entries.cost: A complete rebuild of the corpus, and the addition of a training / held-out split.
entries.heldBy: les trois moitiés du corpus ne partagent aucune formulation

entries.headline: The small model looked incapable of reading an identity number; it was the scorer counting a space as an error.
entries.claimed: The small model cannot read an identity number — 0 %, not a low score.
entries.actually: 63 %. The scorer counted « IT - 5560 - K » as a failure against « IT-5560-K »: it was measuring formatting, not content.
entries.caughtBy: The failure gallery, on its first run.
entries.cost: 133 of 685 recorded failures were false. One field went from 51.7 % to 100 % after the fix.
entries.heldBy: formatting is not counted as an error
entries.reachUncertain: Nothing establishes that this claim was ever published or spoken. Marked as seen out of caution, following the doubt rule above.

entries.headline: The large model was announced as worse than the small one on two fields; the gap was significant on neither.
entries.claimed: The large model is worse than the small one on two fields out of five.
entries.actually: On a single field — and on 120 cases the gap was 4.2 points with intervals that almost entirely overlapped. The claim was not merely miscounted, it was unsupported.
entries.caughtBy: The validation dossier generator, whose « what the sample cannot decide » section listed the pair.
entries.cost: A public post title, pulled a few hours before it went out.
entries.heldBy: à écart non significatif, le moins cher est retenu

entries.headline: On the generative ladder, « bigger is worse » was presented as a fact; the sample did not support it.
entries.claimed: On the generative ladder, bigger is worse on one task and better on the other.
entries.actually: The first half holds — 82.5 % against 95.8 % on address, a real gap. The second does not: between 4B and 8B, classification does not move measurably.
entries.caughtBy: The significance test, applied to all four claims at once.
entries.cost: A sentence already given aloud as settled.
entries.heldBy: un palier plus gros n'est pas supposé meilleur

entries.headline: Three figures on the page were typed by hand and wrong.
entries.claimed: 79.7 % — no: « 83 % against 68 % and 63 % » on the document number.
entries.actually: 79.7 % against 64.4 % and 57.7 %. All three figures were right the day they were written and became wrong at the thousand-case re-measurement, inside a sentence nothing regenerated.
entries.caughtBy: A check written that day, which refuses any hand-typed number in the prose.
entries.cost: Three wrong figures online for a few hours.
entries.heldBy: aucun chiffre n'est tapé à la main dans la prose du README

entries.headline: Latency was measured while playing no part in the routing, though the page claimed otherwise.
entries.claimed: Latency is measured but plays no part in the routing.
entries.actually: True in the morning and false by evening: a budget in seconds now exists and it is the one that binds, not the money. The page contradicted itself from one section to the next.
entries.caughtBy: The audit of the bold claims against the tests that hold them.
entries.cost: A contradiction visible on the published page.
entries.heldBy: le budget de temps mord avant le budget d'argent

entries.headline: A display defect was announced across nine published demos; it affected one.
entries.claimed: The overflow defect affects all nine published demos.
entries.actually: One. The other eight carried the same stylesheet and did not overflow: a parent without padding was also required.
entries.caughtBy: Checking the claim, after making it.
entries.cost: Nothing, except the accuracy of a sentence said too quickly.
entries.notHeld: The claim was about nine published repositories, not this one: no test in this suite can hold it. The check that would catch it here — the overflow detector in `verifier-ecran.mjs` — covers only this screen, and runs with `npm run pages`, not with `npm test`.

entries.headline: The published latencies passed for the models'; they were the models' plus a forgotten audio driver holding one core of ten for sixteen days, worth a third of the total.
entries.claimed: The published latencies are the models', measured one item at a time on an idle machine.
entries.actually: They were the models' **plus an audio driver nobody had looked at**. `UA Mixer Engine` held one core of ten for sixteen days; stopping it removed 22 to 36 % of every tier's latency, and took the retained chain from 1,341 to 968 ms. The accuracies stayed identical across all 35 tier×field combinations: nothing of the model had changed.
entries.caughtBy: A pass contaminated by my own concurrent work, which made `gen-8b` 32 % slower and made me record machine load for the first time.
entries.cost: Three measurement passes. And the section « a tier that vanished between two measurements », which told a story of unstable models where there was only a busy machine: `gen-0.6b` measured at 2,098 ms under a load of 7.98, 1,676 under 4.31, 1,167 under 2.54, against a 2,000 ms ceiling.
entries.heldBy: chaque latence enregistrée dit sous quelle charge elle a été prise

entries.headline: « Nothing leaves your machine » was true by default and false the moment an environment variable pointed at a remote server — the condition was written nowhere.
entries.claimed: Everything runs locally. No API key, nothing leaves the machine.
entries.actually: True by default, false on a configuration nothing forbade. A measurement's path contains exactly one outbound call — the generative host — and `OLLAMA_HOST` is an environment variable: pointed at a team server, every document goes to that third party. The promise was conditional and its condition was written nowhere.
entries.caughtBy: The inventory of everything that can open a connection in `src/`, made in order to turn the claim into proof.
entries.cost: Nothing yet: no real file had been measured. It is the only one of the three taken before it had cost anything.
entries.heldBy: une mesure ne peut contacter que cette machine

entries.headline: Two successive explanations of the same observation — unstable models, then the effect of load — both plausible, both wrong.
entries.claimed: Twice running, a plausible explanation of the same observation: first that the generative tiers were unstable from pass to pass, then that their latency followed machine load.
entries.actually: Both were wrong. The tiers are deterministic — 35 tier×field combinations identical to the thousandth across four passes. And load does not explain the gap: measured deliberately under a load of 8.35, `gen-0.6b` returns 1,654 ms where the original point claimed 2,098 ms under 7.98. The cause was an audio driver, `UA Mixer Engine`, holding one core of ten for sixteen days; stopping it removed 22 to 36 % of latency from every tier.
entries.caughtBy: An experiment built to reproduce the missing point, which returned the opposite verdict to the one it was meant to confirm.
entries.cost: A sales-page section retired twice: « a rival that vanished between two measurements », then « admissibility flips with load ». The second was better supported than the first and wrong for the same reason — one of its three points carried it, and that point was in no file.
entries.heldBy: chaque latence enregistrée dit sous quelle charge elle a été prise

entries.headline: A prompt was declared « retained » for each generative tier on a margin of one field extraction out of six hundred.
entries.claimed: Each generative tier had a formulation chosen for it on the tuning split: `A-sans-exemple` for gen-0.6b and gen-4b, `B-exemple-apparie` for gen-8b. The file wrote them under a key named `retenu` — retained — with no interval and no test.
entries.actually: The selector took the maximum of five rates. The winners beat their runners-up by 12, 1 and 3 field extractions out of 600 — for gen-4b, `A-sans-exemple` at 99.3 % over `C-minimal` at 99.2 %, which is a single extraction. Nothing in the file said so, and nothing could: the script kept only rates, so the margins were not even recoverable from it. A maximum over five noisy numbers is a choice dressed as a measurement.
entries.caughtBy: A paired test run for a different question, whose data made the margins visible — and then by checking which formulation was actually the runner-up before drawing any conclusion from it.
entries.cost: Nothing published: no artefact consumed `retenu`. But the three assignments were reported as results to the person running the project and to the session coordinating it, and the held-out re-measurement they were meant to feed was planned on their basis.
entries.heldBy: departager ne retient rien quand le vainqueur n'est pas séparable de son second

entries.headline: Two confident explanations of prompt behaviour, given without measuring, both wrong.
entries.claimed: First, that `B-exemple-apparie` lost accuracy on the birth field because the model reformatted its answer to match the example's date style. Second, that gen-0.6b collapses without an example because a small model needs one to understand the task.
entries.actually: The first was refuted by looking: 52 of 55 failures are corrupted output, not reformatting — `1 August 1955` came back as `1 August 1:55`. The second is contradicted by the same table it was read from: `A-sans-exemple` contains no example and is the best formulation gen-0.6b has, at 83.5 %.
entries.caughtBy: Being told to check the first before building on it, and by reading the column that disproved the second.
entries.cost: Two mechanisms offered as understanding. Both were the kind of explanation that sounds like knowledge of how models work and is actually a story fitted to one number.
entries.notHeld: No test holds this one. It is not a claim about the code but about the habit of explaining a number before measuring it — the same measurement that refutes such a story would have prevented it, and there is nothing to assert in between.

entries.headline: A decisive paired test, run on the wrong pair, about to be reported as validating a choice it never examined.
entries.claimed: Nearly: that the per-tier formulations survived a paired test. McNemar separated `A-sans-exemple` from `reference` on gen-4b, 32–1, p = 8e-9, and separated them the other way on gen-8b, 45–1. Two decisive p-values, sitting right next to the question of whether the tuning choice held.
entries.actually: Neither test touches the tuning decision. gen-4b's runner-up was `C-minimal`, not `reference`; gen-8b's winner was `B-exemple-apparie`, which was not in the run at all. The comparison measured was winner against third place, and loser against second. The p-values are correct and answer nothing that was asked.
entries.caughtBy: Reading the runner-up out of the tuning file before writing the sentence, instead of after.
entries.cost: None. It was checked inside the same minute it was computed, and never left the session.
entries.notHeld: No test holds this one. Nothing in a repository can check that a correct statistic was applied to the pair somebody actually asked about; only reading the question again does that.
